You have a signed Release of Information.
You reach out to another provider treating the same client.
Then you hear: “We’ll need our own release before the provider can speak with you.”
Another form. Another delay. *Then the phone tag begins.*
You call while they’re with a patient.
They call while you’re in session.
Days pass.
No one is doing anything wrong. We’re all trying to protect our clients and follow the requirements of our respective practices and organizations.
But the process is incredibly fragmented.

**For other clinicians: What part of care coordination creates the most friction for you?**

Hi! If you ever need support with billing, credentialing, live phone answering, email/calendar management, or other general admin tasks for your practice, I highly recommend Virtual Strategies Assistants. You can reach out or schedule a discovery call at www.virtualstrategiesassistants.com

items.text:
"Self-managed" is one of those aged care labels that sounds clearer than it is.

Two providers can both offer self-management and give you quite different levels of control.

Before choosing one, ask:

Can I choose my own workers?
Can I arrange shifts directly?
Can I use third-party workers?
Can I pay for an approved item/service and be reimbursed?
What do you add to third-party invoices?

Under the current Support at Home rules, a provider can charge an overhead for third-party workers, but that overhead is capped at 10% of the actual third-party service cost. 

Care management also still applies when you self-manage.

Get the answers in writing before signing anything.

As fall sets in and the final quarter of the year arrives, staying on top of your Accounts Receivable (A/R) is the single best way to protect your revenue. Waiting until December to review aging claims often means leaving money on the table.

Here are 5 key reasons why consistent A/R tracking is essential right now:

Beat Strict Timely Filing Limits: Insurance payers enforce tight deadlines for initial claims, corrections, and appeals. Catching 60+, 90+, and 120+ day balances now ensures you have enough time to appeal and collect before claims expire permanently.

Prepare for Patient Deductible Resets: Patients scramble to schedule appointments before their coverage resets on January 1st. Clear A/R tracking keeps your patient statements up to date so co-pays and deductibles don't fall behind.

Uncover and Fix Payer Denial Trends: Detailed tracking highlights patterns—like recurring missing documentation or specific clearinghouse delays—allowing you to fix root causes rather than endlessly chasing individual denials.

Stabilize Year-End Cash Flow: Uncollected claims stall your practice's income stream. Cleaning up aging accounts late in the year gives you the predictable cash flow needed for annual bonuses, tax prep, and operating expenses.

Start the New Year with a Clean Slate: Wiping out outdated balances now means you won't enter January bogged down by old debt, letting your staff focus on growth and patient care in the new year.

Don't let your hard-earned revenue drift into next year. Let’s clean up your accounts receivable and make sure every claim gets paid! 📊💰

We should not simply change or delete the CPT code unless we confirm the original coding was incorrect and another code accurately reflects the service provided.
